tape.label: Euribor 12-month
tape.plain: The interest rate most Spanish variable-rate mortgages are priced off. When this rises, monthly repayments follow.

tape.label: ECB mortgage rate (Spain)
tape.plain: The interest rate banks are charging on new mortgages to households, sourced from the ECB's Monetary Interest Rates dataset.

tape.label: Harmonised Consumer Price Index - actual rents
tape.plain: The harmonised index of consumer prices for actual rents on housing, set to 100 in a base year. Shows tenant-cost trend across the Eurozone.

tape.label: Harmonised Consumer Price Index - maintenance and repair
tape.plain: The harmonised index of consumer prices for housing maintenance and repair costs, set to 100 in a base year. Renovation spending moves before property transactions do.

tape.label: House price index
tape.plain: The official measure of how house prices are moving, set to 100 in a base year.

tape.label: New mortgage rate
tape.plain: The interest rate banks are charging on new mortgages.

signals.label: Eviction search attention
signals.plain: How often people across Spain look up evictions. Worry and legal research, not evictions themselves.

signals.label: Job postings index
signals.plain: Index level of total job postings on Indeed for Spain (100 = February 2020), seasonally adjusted and 7-day lagged. A forward-looking indicator of hiring intent.
signals.note: Indeed publishes daily observations for both 'total postings' and 'new postings'; we use 'total postings'. The index is seasonally adjusted. February 2020 baseline = 100. Recent months are withheld until Indeed's data is complete (before the month ends).

signals.label: Building permit visas (new construction buildings)
signals.plain: How many buildings received construction permits for new housing — the earliest signal of supply arriving.

signals.label: Hardship attention (Euribor, eviction, benefits)
signals.plain: How often people look up Euribor, evictions, mortgages and unemployment benefits. Worry, not hardship itself.

signals.label: Relocation attention (padrón, NIE, visas)
signals.plain: How often people look up residency registration, visas and foreigner ID — the paperwork of moving to Spain.

top.label: Room-vs-flat search spread
top.plain: How often people search for a room compared with a whole flat. Rising means households are compressing — taking a room because a flat is out of reach.

top.label: New vehicle registrations
top.plain: How many vehicles were newly registered — a fast, keyless read on household and business confidence.
top.note: Not "new cars sold". Counts DGT transaction code 1 ("Matriculación ordinaria y de ciclomotores") only — genuine new registrations, never transfers of ownership, temporary plates, re-registrations or de-registrations, which are separate transaction codes and excluded. But that transaction code spans nearly every vehicle class, not cars alone: in a sampled month, passenger cars were about 69% of qualifying rows, motorcycles and mopeds about 14%, vans about 9%, and the remainder trucks, buses, trailers, agricultural machinery and a handful of historic and special vehicles. The province is where the registration was filed (DGT's own COD_PROVINCIA_MAT), not the vehicle owner's home province (COD_PROVINCIA_MAT and COD_PROVINCIA_VEH are different fields in the source file) — Madrid runs 3-4x above Barcelona because national fleet, leasing and rental-car operators file their registrations there administratively regardless of where the vehicle will actually operate. That is a real, widely-reported feature of Spanish registration statistics, not a data error: this adapter's province-level annual totals were cross-checked against DGT's own published "Matriculación por provincias" table and matched to within the one month DGT itself never published.

top.label: Foreign interest ratio
top.plain: Non-Spanish-language Wikipedia views about this city, divided by Spanish-language views — a rising ratio means the world is paying more attention than Spain itself.
top.note: Computed as (sum of non-Spanish language edition views) ÷ (Spanish Wikipedia views) × 100. A rising ratio signals rising foreign interest; the absolute value is harder to interpret because it depends on platform-wide usage patterns. Used to track whether a city's interest is shifting toward or away from foreign origin markets (relocation, tourism, investment).

top.label: Souvenir retail concentration
top.plain: Souvenir shops per 100 pharmacies — a ratio that reveals touristification rather than size.
top.note: Numerator: shop=gift (souvenir and gift shops). Denominator: amenity=pharmacy. Spanish pharmacies are licence-capped by law (minimum distance rules, population-based allocation), so their count is pinned to legally-recognised residential population and controlled by the same volunteer mapper pool. This makes pharmacy count an unusually stable denominator that absorbs mapping-effort variation. Rising ratio indicates a neighbourhood is shifting from residential to tourist-serving retail. Discriminates between Central Madrid (high touristification) and outer residential districts.
